title: Professional standard of care
text: A health practitioner must perform duties with the accuracy and honesty the profession requires, follow recognised scientific and technical standards, give the patient due care and comply with applicable laws.
quote: must perform the duties of his job with the level of accuracy and honesty as required by the profession

title: Practise within grade and specialisation
text: The physician must follow the rules, systems and procedures for practising the profession according to grade and specialisation.

title: Record the patient's condition and history before diagnosis and treatment
text: Before diagnosis and treatment the physician must record the patient's health condition and personal and family medical history. MEDIMCOM uses this as the legal basis for requiring allergies, current treatments and pregnancy status before a prescription is cleared.

title: Use the diagnosis and treatment methods the condition requires
text: The physician must use the diagnostic and treatment methods required by the patient's condition.

title: Inform the patient of treatment options
text: The physician must keep the patient informed of the available treatment options.

title: Written prescription with dose and usage
text: The physician must prescribe the medicine, its dose and method of use in writing, with the physician's name, signature and date, and explain the importance of the treatment to the patient or family.

title: Inform the patient about the nature and seriousness of the condition
text: The physician must inform the patient of the nature and seriousness of the condition unless this would harm the patient or the patient cannot cope psychologically; family is informed when the patient lacks capacity or cannot be told.

title: Inform about complications before intervention
text: Before an intervention the physician must inform the patient or family of possible complications, and identify and treat complications where possible.

title: No treatment without consent, except emergencies
text: Treating a patient without consent is prohibited, except where emergency intervention is required and consent cannot be obtained, or where the disease is infectious or threatens public health or safety.
quote: Treat a patient without his consent except in the cases requiring emergent medical intervention

title: No prescription before clinical examination; distance health services
text: Prescribing any treatment before a clinical examination of the patient is prohibited; the health authorities may set a system for providing distance (remote) health services.
quote: Prescribe any treatment before carrying out the clinical examination of the patient.

title: No unnecessary procedures without informed consent
text: Performing unnecessary medical procedures or surgeries without the patient's informed consent is prohibited.

title: Definition of medical error
text: Defines medical error, the basis of a practitioner's liability. It addresses the practitioner's error; it does not allocate responsibility for an AI suggestion validated by the practitioner.

title: Written consent for surgery
text: Written consent of the patient is required for surgical interventions.

title: No abortion and no prescription that may cause abortion (limited exceptions)
text: A doctor may neither perform an abortion nor prescribe anything that may cause abortion of a pregnant woman. Exceptions: (1) danger to the mother's life with no other means, decided by an obstetrician with the treating doctor and a written report signed by the spouses; (2) proven serious, incurable fetal deformity, with written consent of both spouses, within 120 days of pregnancy and confirmed by a medical committee.
quote: A doctor may neither conduct any abortion operation nor prescribe anything that may cause the abortion

title: Disciplinary sanctions including licence suspension
text: Provides for disciplinary measures against practitioners, including suspension of the licence.

title: Mandatory civil liability insurance
text: Insurance against civil liability for medical errors is mandatory.

title: Confidentiality, integrity and availability of health data
text: When using ICT in health: (1) keep health data confidential and do not circulate it outside permitted cases; (2) ensure its validity and credibility by protecting it from unauthorised damage, amendment, alteration, deletion or addition; (3) ensure availability to authorised persons.
quote: To ensure the validity and credibility of the health data and information

title: Health data may not be stored or processed outside the State
text: Health data relating to health services provided in the UAE may not be stored, processed, generated or transferred outside the State, except where a resolution is issued by the Health Authority in coordination with the Ministry. (MEDIMCOM interpretation, not the text: sending consultation content to a cloud AI service hosted abroad is processing outside the State.)
quote: It is not permissible to store, process, generate or transform the health data and information outside State

title: Use of patient information only for health purposes without written approval
text: Patient information must be kept confidential and used only for health purposes without the patient's written approval, except: (1) insurers or funders reviewing entitlements; (2) scientific and clinical research without disclosing identity; (3) preventive and curative public-health measures or protecting the patient or contacts; (4) request of judicial authorities; (5) Health Authority request for monitoring, inspection and public health.

title: Retention of health data for at least 25 years
text: Health data kept through ICT must be retained for a period commensurate with need and not less than 25 years from the last health procedure, with confidentiality, validity and credibility ensured.

title: Penalty for violating the localisation rule
text: Violating Article 13 is punishable by a fine of AED 500,000 to AED 700,000.

title: Exceptions allowing health data outside the UAE
text: Health data may be stored or transferred abroad in listed cases, including: treatment of the patient abroad; samples sent to foreign laboratories; scientific research under UAE rules; UAE insurers needing data abroad with patient consent; requests by cooperating competent authorities; simple personal medical devices; pharmacovigilance; and other cases approved by the health authorities.

title: Conditions on permitted transfers
text: Permitted transfers remain subject to controls reported as: written patient consent, limits on sharing, encryption to best standards, and a copy of the data stored inside the country.

title: Scope exclusions: government data and regulated health data
text: The decree-law does not apply to government data or to personal health data that has its own legislation regulating its protection and processing. Health data in MEDIMCOM is therefore governed first by Federal Law No. 2 of 2019.

title: Right to object to automated decisions
text: A data subject may object to decisions based on automated processing, including profiling, that have legal or seriously adverse effects, unless the processing is agreed in a contract, required by law, or consented to in advance.

title: Cross-border transfer of (non-health) personal data
text: Transfers are allowed to countries with adequate protection or under agreements (Art. 22); otherwise under contractual safeguards or explicit consent where not contrary to public or security interests (Art. 23).

title: AI-based products can be medical equipment
text: Medical Equipment is a medical product containing a substance, device, instrument, implant or system, including accessories and operating software, and includes wearable devices and products based on AI technology.
quote: shall include wearable devices and products based on AI technology

title: A prescription is issued by a licensed practitioner
text: A prescription is a document issued by a licensed practitioner to a practitioner authorised to dispense; verbal orders must later be documented as set by ministerial resolution.

title: Marketing approval required
text: Importing, distributing, selling, using or manufacturing medical products for circulation is prohibited without marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment.

title: Emergency use approval
text: The decree-law provides for emergency use approval of medical products.

title: Prescribing only when authorised
text: Licensed health practitioners may not advise on, prescribe or dispense medical products unless authorised under the decree-law and its regulations.

title: Controlled products only on a licensed human physician's prescription
text: Pharmacists may dispense controlled products for patients only on a prescription from a licensed human physician (separate rules for veterinary use).

title: Right to communicate and to information through sign language and other means
text: People of determination have the right to express themselves and to seek, receive and impart information on an equal footing, using Braille, sign language and other means of communication.

title: Health and rehabilitation services
text: People of determination are entitled to health and rehabilitation services, at the State's expense, as set out by the law.

title: Substitute means of communication
text: The law provides for substitute (alternative) means of communication for people of determination.

title: Simplified materials
text: Provides for simplified materials adapted to people of determination.

title: Duty to notify communicable diseases
text: Physicians, pharmacists and other practitioners must notify their supervising body no later than 24 hours after knowing or suspecting a Group (A) disease listed in Schedule 1; other persons (contacts, supervisors, facility managers) must notify immediately.

title: Notification by health bodies and facilities
text: The Ministry, health bodies and private health facilities must notify immediately and no later than 24 hours for Group (A) diseases and 7 days for Group (B) diseases.

title: Immediate action and cooperation of health facilities
text: On notification, the Ministry and health body act immediately (isolation where needed, testing, referral); health facilities must fully cooperate by providing diagnosis, treatment and follow-up information.

title: Powers during an epidemic
text: During an epidemic the Ministry and health body, with the concerned bodies, may declare an infected area, regulate entry and exit, restrict gatherings, regulate public places and apply measures to patients, suspects and contacts.

title: Confidentiality of infected persons' information
text: Infected persons are entitled to confidentiality of their disease-related information, which may be disclosed only in cases prescribed by law.

title: AI supports; a human decides
text: AI in healthcare is treated as supportive technology: it requires a human to make final decisions and be responsible for any actions taken by the technology.
quote: it requires a human to make final decisions and be responsible for any actions taken by the technology

title: Verifiable and explainable AI; developers accountable
text: AI software should be verifiable and explainable; developers are accountable; major versions require certification and re-certification; validation must be auditable; regular audits and feedback to DoH.

title: Graceful degradation
text: AI solutions should degrade gracefully when components fail, so that care continues safely.

title: Clinicians keep ultimate decision-making authority
text: Clinicians should retain ultimate decision-making authority in all AI-assisted healthcare scenarios.
quote: Clinicians should retain ultimate decision-making authority in all AI-assisted healthcare scenarios.

title: Inform patients when AI contributes to decisions
text: Systems must include mechanisms to inform patients when AI contributes to clinical or operational decisions, including its function, limitations and intended outcomes.

title: Consent mechanisms and opt-out for AI-driven services
text: Clear consent mechanisms must ensure informed decision-making and transparency; patients are told they can opt out of AI-driven services where applicable.

title: All decisions logged and traceable
text: All decisions, changes, updates and interventions must be logged and traceable to a responsible party.
quote: All decisions, changes, updates, and interventions must be logged and traceable to a responsible party.

title: Report adverse outcomes and ethical concerns
text: Governance includes reporting adverse outcomes or ethical concerns to governance bodies.

title: Compute and storage in the UAE
text: Compute and storage infrastructure, including disaster-recovery sites, must be located in the UAE; remote access for development and support teams should be exclusively from within the UAE.

title: Datasets reflect population diversity
text: All training, validation and test datasets must reflect the diversity of the target population.

title: Validation before deployment
text: AI models shall undergo rigorous validation against established performance benchmarks before deployment.

title: Risk classes: very high risk prohibited, high risk assessed
text: AI systems with very high residual risk must be prohibited from deployment; high-risk systems require conformity assessments before and after deployment.

title: Supportive technology needs a human final decision
text: Supportive technology requires a human to make final decisions and be responsible for any actions taken by the technology.

title: Accountability and appeals
text: Accountability for outcomes of an AI solution must be agreed; developers are accountable to end users; solutions must have built-in appeal procedures so users can challenge significant decisions.

title: Failures traced, diagnosed and controlled
text: Developers must build systems whose failures can be traced, diagnosed and controlled.

title: Mandatory disclosure, including the professional's role
text: AI solutions must disclose, among other items, their AI-enabled functions, validation, data sets, algorithm type, the role of the healthcare professional in the final decision and the limitations of data and algorithms.

title: Independent third-party validation
text: All AI solutions for healthcare must undergo independent validation by a competent third party.

title: Supervised by end users; can be overridden
text: AI solutions must be safe, secure and supervised by end users, and must be able to be overridden or their decisions reversed by designated end users.

title: Auditable validation statements
text: AI tools must include auditable validation statements.

title: Incident reporting and independent audits
text: Adverse events should be reported in a timely way to oversight bodies; all known or suspected AI incidents or deficiencies, and issues that may affect patient safety, are reported to DHA; regular independent audits are conducted.

title: No narcotic, controlled or semi-controlled medicines via telehealth
text: The physician shall not prescribe narcotic, controlled or semi-controlled medication through telehealth services.
quote: The physician shall not prescribe Narcotic, Controlled or Semi-controlled medication through telehealth services.

title: Telehealth prescriptions follow the MOHAP drug list and an online prescription system
text: Prescribing via telehealth follows the UAE MOHAP drug list, and prescriptions must be issued through an online prescription system with electronic transfer.

title: Telehealth consent documented at each encounter
text: The professional obtains and documents consent from the patient or guardian; electronic consent is acceptable; consent for treatment must be documented at each encounter.

title: Patient identification with at least three identifiers
text: The patient is identified with at least three identifiers (e.g. full name, date of birth, Emirates ID, record number, phone), and identity is verified and consent granted before diagnosis.

title: Documentation and 25-year retention
text: All telehealth encounters are documented in the medical record (service type, participants' licence numbers, locations, confirmation of consent) and retained for at least 25 years.

title: Telehealth data stays in the UAE
text: Telehealth data is stored with a cloud service provider in the UAE; storing, developing or transferring health data outside the country is not permitted unless applicable law allows.

title: People of determination and understandable language
text: Provisions must be in place for People of Determination and access must not exclude them; consultations are offered at least in Arabic and English, interpretation services are encouraged, and information is given in a language the patient easily understands.

title: Emergency protocols in telehealth
text: Providers must have tested written protocols for emergency requests, emergency contact numbers, and must not delay advice to seek emergency services.

title: Explain limits of prescribing without tests
text: Limitations of prescribing without confirmatory laboratory testing must be explained to the patient.

title: Abu Dhabi tele-medicine services
text: The DOH Standard on Tele-Medicine (effective 16 September 2020) covers tele-diagnosis, tele-counseling, tele-medical interventions, tele-consultation, tele-prescription and tele-monitoring, and applies to DOH-licensed or approved facilities.
quote: Healthcare facilities licensed or approved by DOH to provide tele-medicine services.

title: Human oversight
text: The Charter affirms the irreplaceable value of human judgment and human oversight over AI.

title: Data privacy and transparency
text: Privacy of community members is a top priority, and AI systems should be understandable in how they operate and decide.

title: Inclusive access and compliance with treaties and laws
text: AI awareness for an inclusive future (equitable access for all segments of society) and commitment to international treaties and local laws.

title: Healthcare is a priority sector; strong governance
text: The strategy names healthcare among priority sectors and sets objectives including providing data and infrastructure to become an AI test bed (7) and ensuring strong governance and effective regulation (8).

title: UAE is a State Party to the CRPD
text: The UAE signed the CRPD on 12 February 2008 and ratified it (Presidential Decree of 24 December 2009); the report's introduction refers to 19 March 2010.

title: Accessible information and alternative communication
text: States provide public information in accessible formats in a timely manner at no extra cost; accept and facilitate sign languages, Braille, augmentative and alternative communication and other accessible means chosen by persons with disabilities in official interactions; recognise and promote sign languages.
quote: Accepting and facilitating the use of sign languages, Braille, augmentative and alternative communication,

title: Accessibility of information and communication
text: Accessibility applies to the physical environment and to information and communications, including technologies and systems.

title: Situations of risk and humanitarian emergencies
text: States take all necessary measures to protect persons with disabilities in situations of risk, including armed conflict, humanitarian emergencies and natural disasters.

title: Legal capacity and support in exercising it
text: Persons with disabilities enjoy legal capacity on an equal basis, and States provide access to the support they may require in exercising it (relevant to consent given through alternative communication).

title: Right to health; care on the basis of free and informed consent
text: Persons with disabilities have the right to the highest attainable standard of health without discrimination; health professionals provide care of the same quality on the basis of free and informed consent.

title: Notify WHO within 24 hours
text: Each State Party notifies WHO, through its National IHR Focal Point, within 24 hours of assessment of events that may constitute a public health emergency of international concern.

title: Confidentiality of personal health information under the IHR
text: Health information about identifiable persons collected or received under the IHR is kept confidential and processed anonymously as required by national law.
quote: which refers to an identified or identifiable person shall be kept confidential

title: WHO principles for AI in health
text: Protect human autonomy; promote human well-being, safety and the public interest; ensure transparency, explainability and intelligibility; foster responsibility and accountability; ensure inclusiveness and equity; promote AI that is responsive and sustainable.

title: Governance of large multi-modal models in health
text: Governments should assign a regulator to assess and approve LMMs for health use, and require independent post-release audits and impact assessments, with results disaggregated by user characteristics such as disability.

title: Human oversight and determination
text: Principle of human oversight and determination: humans may rely on AI for efficiency, but an AI system can never replace ultimate human responsibility and accountability.
quote: an AI system can never replace ultimate human responsibility and accountability

title: Automatic logging over the lifetime
text: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over their lifetime, to detect risks and substantial modifications and support post-market monitoring.
quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.

title: Human oversight, including awareness of automation bias
text: High-risk AI systems are designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them, prevent or minimise risks to health, safety and fundamental rights, remain aware of automation bias, and decide not to use or to override the output.

title: AI regulatory sandboxes and use of personal data in them
text: Member States set up AI regulatory sandboxes; personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be used in a sandbox only for substantial public interest (including public health), when anonymised or synthetic data cannot meet the need, in an isolated environment, with logs, no effects on data subjects and deletion at the end.

title: Reporting serious incidents
text: Providers of high-risk AI systems report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities immediately once a causal link is established or reasonably likely, and no later than 15 days after becoming aware (shorter limits for widespread or fatal incidents).

title: Software is a product; disclosure and presumption of defect
text: Software, including AI and software-as-a-service, is a product for strict liability; courts can order disclosure of evidence (Art. 9) and presume defectiveness when evidence is not disclosed or safety requirements are breached (Art. 10).
quote: includes electricity, digital manufacturing files, raw materials and software

title: Decision-support software classified at least class IIa
text: Software intended to provide information used to take decisions with diagnostic or therapeutic purposes is at least class IIa (higher if decisions may cause serious harm or death).

title: Equivalent access to emergency services for persons with disabilities
text: Member States ensure that end-users with disabilities have access to emergency services through emergency communications equivalent to that enjoyed by other end-users.

title: When decision-support software is not a device
text: Software is non-device clinical decision support when it (1) does not analyse medical images or signals, (2) displays or analyses medical information, (3) supports a health professional's recommendations, and (4) lets the professional independently review the basis of recommendations without relying primarily on them; the 2026 revision places automation-bias concerns under criterion 4.

title: Avoid NSAIDs from 20 weeks of pregnancy
text: Avoid NSAIDs at 20 weeks or later in pregnancy unless specifically advised by a health professional; does not apply to low-dose aspirin; other medicines such as acetaminophen (paracetamol) are available for pain and fever.
quote: Other medicines, such as acetaminophen, are available to treat pain and fever during pregnancy.

title: Misoprostol can cause abortion
text: Misoprostol administered to pregnant women can cause birth defects, abortion, premature birth or uterine rupture; patients must be advised of its abortifacient property.
quote: CAN CAUSE BIRTH DEFECTS, ABORTION, PREMATURE BIRTH OR UTERINE RUPTURE.

title: Identify, record, flag, share and meet communication needs
text: Since 1 August 2016, organisations providing NHS or publicly funded adult social care must identify, record, flag, share and meet the information and communication support needs of people with a disability, impairment or sensory loss.

title: Regulatory sandbox for AI medical devices
text: A regulatory sandbox pilot launched in 2024 to identify and address challenges of regulating standalone AI medical devices used in NHS settings, informing future guidance.

title: Testing comprehension of graphical symbols
text: Specifies a method of testing what proportion of people comprehend a graphical symbol correctly, used to choose the most comprehensible variant.

title: ML pipeline architecture
text: Defines an architectural framework for machine learning in future networks, including an ML pipeline and ML management and orchestration functions, and how to integrate them.

title: ITU AI readiness factors
text: Preliminary readiness factors: data, research, deployment support, standards, open source and code, sandbox environments.

title: AI readiness factors (Report 2.0)
text: Six readiness factors: data (availability and quality of datasets), research (collaboration between domain and AI research), deployment support (physical, communication and backend infrastructure), standards (trust, interoperability, compliance), open source and code, sandbox environments for experimentation and validation.

title: Human interface
text: Ease of human interaction with AI systems; metrics include AI-supported interfaces and interaction channels, local-language model availability, usability, cultural sensitivity and safety safeguards.

title: Collaboration with AI
text: Human-AI co-creation and shared decision-making; metrics include feedback loops, trust metrics and comparison of co-created output with human-only or AI-only baselines.

title: AI and policies
text: Testing policies in sandboxes and ensuring policies enable AI integration; metrics include vertical sandboxes and domain-specific policy evaluation, simulation of policy impacts, horizontal policies on data, AI lifecycle and explainability, policy briefs, audits and data sovereignty.

title: AI for inclusion
text: Using AI to bridge social divides, including accessibility; metrics include edge AI with privacy and low latency, generative AI support for sign languages and regional languages, offline kits and number of beneficiaries.

title: African Union continental AI strategy
text: Endorsed in July 2024; promotes ethical, responsible and equitable AI, unified national approaches and inclusive AI development; names healthcare among sectors transformed by AI.

title: Cameroon: practice of medicine reserved to registered physicians (comparative)
text: Cameroon's 1990 law organises the medical profession (registration with the Order of Physicians); article-level content to be re-read before citation.

title: Cameroon: personal data protection law applicable from 23 June 2026 (comparative)
text: Cameroon's 2024 personal data law, applicable from 23 June 2026, regulates processing and cross-border transfers; article-level content to be re-read before citation.

title: Practice of medicine reserved to physicians registered with the Order
text: No one may practise medicine in Cameroon unless registered on the roll of the Ordre national des médecins.
quote: Nul ne peut exercer la profession de médecin au Cameroun s'il n'est pas inscrit au tableau de l'Ordre.

title: Physicians bound by professional secrecy
text: A physician practising in public administration or the private sector is bound by professional secrecy (scope defined elsewhere).

title: Illegal practice of medicine and penalties
text: Illegal practice includes an unauthorised person habitually taking part in diagnosis or treatment, even in a doctor's presence; penalties: 6 days to 6 months' imprisonment and/or a fine of 200,000 to 2,000,000 FCFA, with immediate cessation.
quote: à l'établissement de diagnostics ou aux traitements d'affections par actes professionnels

title: Consent to personal data processing
text: Consent to processing must be free, informed, specific, unambiguous and express, obtained before processing; parental consent for minors under 18.

title: Health data are sensitive data
text: Sensitive data, including health data, may in principle not be processed, except on listed legal bases such as the protection of health.

title: Transfers of personal data outside Cameroon
text: Transfers of personal data to another country require appropriate safeguards and, according to secondary sources, prior authorisation of the data protection authority.

title: Personal data protection authority
text: Creates an independent data protection authority; its organisation is to be set by presidential decree.

title: Sanctions for breaches
text: Administrative fines up to 1 billion FCFA for the most serious breaches; criminal sanctions also apply (unauthorised processing, illegal transfers).

title: Compliance deadline
text: Data controllers had 18 months from promulgation (23 December 2024), i.e. until 23 June 2026, to comply.

title: Deaf persons are persons with a sensory disability
text: Sensory disabilities include deaf, deaf-mute, mute and hard-of-hearing persons.
quote: sourds, sourds - muets, muets, malentendants

title: State coverage of health care for eligible persons with disabilities
text: Indigent persons holding a national disability card receive total or partial State coverage of rehabilitation, consultations, laboratory tests, imaging, hospitalisation, evacuations and some medicines.
quote: une prise en charge totale ou partielle par l'état

title: Access of persons with disabilities to information technologies
text: The State, decentralised authorities and civil society must facilitate access of persons with disabilities to information technologies.
quote: L'accès des personnes handicapées aux technologies de l'information

title: Medical ethics: consent, information, prescription, secrecy
text: The code of medical ethics governs consent to care, information of the patient, written prescriptions and medical secrecy; article numbers to be read before citation.

title: Pharmacy and medicines
text: Organises the pharmacy profession; marketing authorisation of medicines to be checked with the national regulator.

title: Criminal sanction of breaches of professional secrecy
text: According to legal doctrine, breaches of medical secrecy are punished under Article 310 of the Penal Code (penalty not read).

title: Tramadol in pregnancy: neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome
text: Prolonged use of tramadol during pregnancy can result in neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening if not recognised and treated; the prescriber should weigh this risk and inform the patient.
quote: Prolonged use of tramadol hydrochloride during pregnancy can result in neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome

title: Tramadol in children and adolescents
text: Tramadol is contraindicated in all children younger than 12 years and after tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy in children younger than 18; its use should be avoided in adolescents 12 to 18 years who have other risk factors.
quote: Avoid the use of tramadol hydrochloride in adolescents 12 to 18 years of age who have other risk factors

title: Tramadol maximum daily dose
text: Tramadol tablets must not be given at a dose exceeding 400 mg per day.
quote: Do not administer tramadol hydrochloride tablets at a dose exceeding 400 mg per day.

title: Metformin maximum daily dose
text: Adults: up to a maximum of 2550 mg per day in divided doses; paediatric patients (10 years and older): up to 2000 mg per day.
quote: up to a maximum dose of 2550 mg per day, given in divided doses.

title: Metformin and renal impairment
text: Metformin is contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2); starting it at an eGFR between 30 and 45 is not recommended; renal function must be assessed before initiation.
quote: Severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2)

title: Metformin and hepatic impairment
text: Metformin is not recommended in patients with hepatic impairment (risk of lactic acidosis).
quote: Metformin Hydrochloride Tablets are not recommended in patients with hepatic impairment.

title: Amoxicillin and beta-lactam hypersensitivity
text: Amoxicillin is contraindicated in patients who have had a serious hypersensitivity reaction to amoxicillin or to other beta-lactam antibacterials (penicillins, cephalosporins).
quote: contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction

title: Amoxicillin and severe renal impairment
text: No dose reduction unless renal impairment is severe; patients with a glomerular filtration rate below 30 mL/min should not receive the 875 mg dose.
quote: Renal impairment patients with a glomerular filtration rate of less than 30 mL/min should NOT receive the 875 mg dose.

title: Acetaminophen: liver warning and maximum daily dose
text: Severe liver damage may occur above 4,000 mg of acetaminophen in 24 hours, with other acetaminophen-containing drugs, or with 3 or more alcoholic drinks a day; ask a doctor before use in liver disease and a doctor or pharmacist when taking warfarin.
quote: more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen in 24 hours

title: Ibuprofen: stomach bleeding and conditions needing a doctor's advice
text: Stomach bleeding risk is higher at age 60 or older, with past stomach ulcers or bleeding problems, or when taking a blood thinning (anticoagulant) or steroid drug; ask a doctor before use with high blood pressure, heart disease, liver cirrhosis, kidney disease, asthma or past stroke.
quote: take a blood thinning (anticoagulant) or steroid drug

title: Ibuprofen: last 3 months of pregnancy
text: It is especially important not to use ibuprofen during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless definitely directed by a doctor.
quote: It is especially important not to use ibuprofen during the last 3 months of pregnancy

title: Ibuprofen maximum daily dose (prescription)
text: Prescription ibuprofen: do not exceed 3200 mg total daily dose.
quote: Do not exceed 3200 mg total daily dose.

title: Aspirin: Reye's syndrome in children and teenagers
text: Children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms should not use aspirin (Reye's syndrome, rare but serious).
quote: Children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms should not use this product.

title: Aspirin: last 3 months of pregnancy
text: It is especially important not to use aspirin during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless definitely directed by a doctor.
quote: It is especially important not to use aspirin during the last 3 months of pregnancy.

title: Aspirin: stomach bleeding and maximum daily dose
text: Stomach bleeding risk is higher with past stomach ulcers or bleeding problems or when taking a blood thinning (anticoagulant) or steroid drug; adults: no more than 12 tablets of 325 mg in 24 hours unless directed by a doctor.
quote: do not take more than 12 tablets in 24 hours unless directed by a doctor
